citation: (1) Agarwal, He, Vasilescu. 'AI IDEs or Autonomous Agents? Measuring the Impact of Coding Agents on Software Development'. arXiv:2601.13597, v1 20 Jan 2026, v2 27 Jan 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13597. (2) Kashif, Li, Liang, Tahir, Feng, Li, Shahin. 'Beyond Functional Correctness: Design Issues in AI IDE-Generated Large-Scale Projects'. arXiv:2604.06373, 7 Apr 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06373. (3) da Mota, Gama. 'Comparing the Quality of Code Generated by Vibe Coding Tools'. arXiv:2608.16302, 17 Aug 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16302. Background only, older than 12 months: Sabra, Schmitt, Tyler, arXiv:2508.14727 (Aug 2025), seen only via search summary.
source_tier: All three are preprints (arXiv, cs.SE); none confirmed as peer-reviewed. [uncertain] whether any has since been accepted at a venue.
access_status: Abstract page only for all three (arXiv abs pages opened via WebFetch, which summarised rather than quoted). Full text NOT read. Sabra et al. 2508.14727: search snippet only. No study found that measures agents suppressing or silencing linters or type checkers.
sponsor_and_incentive: No funding statement found on the abstract pages of any of the three. [uncertain] for full text. Academic authors; no vendor incentive evident.
exact_quotes: Only one short verbatim excerpt obtained, from the abstract of 2608.16302: 'Lovable concentrates issues of lower severity but presents a substantially higher density of code smells per KLOC.' No other verbatim quotes; remaining content is paraphrase from the fetch tool's summary. [uncertain]
date_and_recency: All three published Jan to Aug 2026, inside the 12-month window ending 2026-10-16. Data collection windows not seen (full text unread). [uncertain]
key_claims: (1) Agarwal et al.: using AIDev data and a staggered difference-in-differences design with matched controls, agent adoption (first agent-generated PR) gives large but short-lived speed gains where the agent is the first AI tool, while quality risks persist; authors call it sustained, agent-induced technical debt. (2) Kashif et al.: Cursor-generated projects were largely functional but carried maintainability and evolvability risks that static analysis surfaced (duplication, high complexity, large methods, exception handling, framework best-practice violations). (3) da Mota and Gama: SonarQube found differing issue profiles across Lovable, v0 and Replit output. Static analysis here is used as a measurement tool, not as a gate the agents were run against. Nothing found on agents gaming or silencing lint or type checks; that half of the brief is unsupported by an opened source.
headline_figures: Agarwal et al.: static-analysis warnings rose by roughly 18%, cognitive complexity by roughly 39% after agent adoption (per abstract summary; comparison is matched controls, monthly repo-level). Kashif et al.: 10 projects, average functional correctness 91%, average 16,965 LOC and 114 files; CodeScene 1,305 design issues in 9 categories; SonarQube 3,193 design issues in 11 categories. da Mota and Gama: 9 web apps (3 tools x 3 projects); no numeric issue counts seen. Exact wording/units not verified against full text. [uncertain]
sample_unit_and_population: Agarwal et al.: open-source GitHub repositories from AIDev dataset; repository counts not seen. Kashif et al.: 10 Cursor-generated projects across 3 domains, human-in-the-loop generation. da Mota and Gama: 9 generated web apps from 3 vibe-coding tools. Very small samples for 2 and 3.
observed_vs_stated: Observed: code and repository measurements by static-analysis tools. No self-reported belief.
what_makes_trust_justified: Agarwal et al. call for quality safeguards, provenance tracking and selective deployment of agents. Kashif et al. imply static analysis plus human review is needed beyond functional tests, since projects scored 91% functional but still had design issues. [uncertain] as inferred from abstracts.
what_it_costs: Not quantified in any source seen.
failure_mode_class: Wrong or low-quality code: maintainability, complexity, duplication (technical debt). Not destructive action or false report.
control_that_would_have_prevented: Not an incident study. Static-analysis gates in CI would flag the issue classes found, but no source shows a gate preventing them.
limitations_stated: Not seen; full texts unread. Obvious limits: preprints, small samples (10 and 9 projects), SonarQube/CodeScene rules are proxies for quality not defects. [uncertain]
counter_evidence: Sabra et al. (background, Aug 2025, snippet only): no direct correlation between functional pass rates and SonarQube issue counts, so passing tests does not imply clean static analysis. Suppression-comment research (Suppressed Static Analysis Warnings, FSE 2025, UBC) concerns human developers and was seen only as a search result; not evidence about agents. Practitioner tools (lazy-ignores linters, a DEV Community post on 'AI makes CI green by cheating') assert agents add noqa/type: ignore comments, but are anecdotal and not opened. Treat agent gaming of linters as unverified.
verification_status: Agarwal et al. 18% and 39% figures: abs page opened, summarised by fetch tool, full text not opened [uncertain]. Kashif et al. figures: abs page opened, figures reported by fetch tool, full text not opened [uncertain]. da Mota and Gama: abs page opened, no figures. Sabra et al.: search snippet only [uncertain]. Agents silencing linters: no primary source opened.
usable_claim: A preprint tracking open-source repositories found static-analysis warnings rose by roughly 18% and cognitive complexity by roughly 39% after agents were adopted. Separate small studies of Cursor and vibe-coding output found static analysis surfaces maintainability issues in code that otherwise works.
do_not_use: Any claim that agents routinely suppress, disable or game linters and type checkers (no opened evidence). Any claim that static analysis catches real bugs or vulnerabilities in agent code (these studies count warnings, not confirmed defects). Figures as peer-reviewed.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Not checked against The Verification Gap or Checking Isn't Catching essays. [uncertain]
